entries.title: Prometheus and Micrometer
entries.body:
Prometheus pulls metrics: every few seconds it scrapes an HTTP endpoint such as Spring Boot's /actuator/prometheus, where Micrometer exposes counters, gauges and histograms.

Counters only go up, so you query their rate: rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[5m]) is requests per second. Gauges are current values, like busy Tomcat threads or active Hikari connections. Without metrics you learn about problems from your users, late and vaguely.

entries.title: The USE method
entries.body:
Brendan Gregg's checklist for finding a bottleneck: for every resource, check Utilization (how busy it is), Saturation (how much work is waiting) and Errors.

Walk the request path: CPU, thread pool, connection pool, database CPU and I/O, disk. The first resource that is saturated is usually the bottleneck; the ones behind it look idle because work cannot reach them. A low CPU next to a full connection pool points at the database, not at the code.
